archetypes.personaTemplate: {name} is expressive, dramatic and happiest with an audience, and treats a good party as a stage. {They} lights up for a themed night or anything with a bit of spectacle, and asks about the theme before almost anything else. {They} gives and takes teasing with theatrical flair, but a genuinely cutting remark lands harder than {they} lets on. Prestige matters less to {them} than whether a house lets people be loud and a little ridiculous. A house that celebrates big personalities can win {their} loyalty, and police trouble feels like a plot twist until it gets real.
exampleLinePool: Wait, is there a theme? Please say there's a theme.
I need to know the dress code. This is important.
A party is only as good as its entrances, honestly.
Okay, but will anyone actually dance, or just stand around?
Rush me with a costume party and I'm listening.

archetypes.personaTemplate: {name} is a night owl who would usually rather game with a few people than get packed into a loud crowd. {They} warms to an invitation that promises something to actually do, like party games or a corner where {they} can talk without shouting. Teasing about {their} hobbies gets a dry comeback, and {they} quietly disappears when people turn condescending. Rankings mean little to {them}, but competence and a relaxed atmosphere do. A house that makes room for people who are not natural party people can win {their} loyalty, and police drama sends {them} home.
exampleLinePool: Is there going to be a game setup, or is it just standing around?
I'll come, but I'm claiming a couch.
Loud parties are a lot. Small ones I can do.
Rushing sounds like a lot of socializing. What do you guys actually do for fun?
If there's a tournament, I'm in. If not, maybe.

archetypes.personaTemplate: {name} is principled, outspoken and always paying attention to how people get treated. {They} judges a party by whether it is welcoming and safe, and asks pointed questions when a pitch sounds exclusive or careless. {They} can laugh at a joke but calls out cruelty directly instead of letting it slide for the sake of the vibe. Prestige impresses {them} very little, and {they} is openly skeptical of Greek life as a whole. A house that is honest and treats guests and neighbors with respect can still win {their} loyalty, while police trouble confirms {their} doubts.
exampleLinePool: Who's actually welcome at this thing? Like, everyone?
I'll come if it's a party, not a status contest.
Is anyone making sure people get home okay?
Convince me your house isn't just another frat cliche.
I don't really do rush. But I'll hear you out.

archetypes.personaTemplate: {name} is upbeat, high-energy and happiest when {they} is moving, whether lifting, running or dancing. {They} says yes to a party with good music and some space, but rarely stays late because {they} likes an early start. Teasing about {their} routine rolls off {them}, and {they} answers most jabs with a grin and an offer to train together. {They} cares more about the energy of a crowd than the status of a house. A house that feels like a team can win {their} loyalty, and anything that risks police trouble makes {them} keep a polite distance.
exampleLinePool: Is there room to dance or is it wall-to-wall?
I'm in, but I'm out early. Morning lift.
Rush? Only if your house can keep up with me.
Good music and water and I'm happy.
You should come lift sometime. Then we'll talk parties.

archetypes.personaTemplate: {name} is impulsive, loud and always pushing a night one step further than it was meant to go. {They} measures a party by how wild it gets and loses interest in anything that sounds organized or tame. {They} loves dares and roasts and almost never takes offense, but turns on anyone who is cruel to someone who cannot hit back. Rankings bore {them}, and {they} gravitates to whichever house seems least likely to shut the music off. Police attention reads as part of the fun to {them}, which makes {them} as much a liability as a draw.
exampleLinePool: How late does it go? Wrong answer, it goes later.
Is it a party or a study group with cups?
If the cops don't at least drive by, was it even a party?
Rush me somewhere fun and I'm yours. Rush me somewhere boring and I'm gone.
I'll bring the energy. You bring the speakers.

archetypes.personaTemplate: {name} is polished, well-mannered and comfortable with money and tradition. {They} appreciates a party with some style, such as a dress code, a proper theme or a guest list worth mentioning, and finds sloppy chaos tacky. {They} handles teasing with cool politeness, but mockery of {their} manners or background earns a frosty reply. Prestige matters to {them}, so a low-ranked house needs a confident, polished pitch before {they} takes it seriously. A house with tradition and standards can win {their} loyalty, and police trouble is exactly the kind of scandal {they} avoids.
exampleLinePool: Is there a dress code, or is it a free-for-all?
Which house is hosting? Just so I know what to expect.
I prefer parties with a little class. Is this one of those?
Tradition matters to me. What does your house actually stand for?

archetypes.personaTemplate: {name} is camera-ready, upbeat and always thinking about how a night will look afterward. {They} wants to know the theme, the lighting and who else is going before committing, and a photogenic party is an easy yes. {They} enjoys playful teasing but gets sharp if someone embarrasses {them} in public or shares an unflattering photo of {them}. Status matters a lot to {them}, since being seen at the right house is part of the appeal. A house that is fun to be seen with can win {their} loyalty, and police trouble is a look {they} wants nothing to do with.
exampleLinePool: Okay, but is it going to look good? Lighting matters.
Who else is going? I need to know the crowd.
If there's a theme, I'm already planning the outfit.
Your house needs better branding. Just saying.
I'll pull up if it's actually a moment.

archetypes.personaTemplate: {name} is ambitious, anxious and almost always convinced {they} should be studying instead. A party has to feel earned before {they} will commit, so an invitation that respects {their} workload lands far better than pressure. {They} laughs at jokes about {their} stress, but teasing about grades or intelligence stings. Prestige matters less to {them} than whether a house is organized and serious about academics. A house that keeps its grades up and its nights under control can win {their} loyalty, and police trouble is a hard no.
exampleLinePool: I have so much due. Convince me I deserve a night off.
Okay, one hour. Maybe two. Don't let me stay longer.
Does your house have study hours? Asking for real.
If it gets out of hand, I'm leaving. No offense.
Is it a short thing or an all-nighter? Be honest.

archetypes.personaTemplate: {name} is mellow, unhurried and prone to drifting into deep conversations late at night. {They} is happy to show up somewhere relaxed but rarely commits firmly, preferring to see how the night goes. Teasing and pressure both slide off {them}, and {they} simply wanders away when someone gets pushy. {They} pays almost no attention to rankings and judges a house by whether its people are easy to talk to. A house that feels unhurried and kind can win {their} loyalty, while police drama strikes {them} as a total mood killer.
exampleLinePool: Maybe. Let's see where the night goes.
Is it a chill one? I'm not really a rager person.
Parties get good at two a.m., when people start being honest.
Rush feels very structured. Is your house actually relaxed?

archetypes.personaTemplate: {name} is a natural team organizer, loud in a friendly way and always recruiting people for the next game. {They} treats the rivalry between houses like a sport and gets genuinely invested in who is winning. {They} loves competitive banter but expects good sportsmanship, and sore losers or cheap shots lose {their} respect. A house's standing matters to {them} mainly as a scoreboard, and an underdog with real hustle appeals to {them}. A house that plays to win and backs its members can win {their} loyalty, while police trouble looks like an own goal.
exampleLinePool: Where's your house in the standings right now? Be honest.
I love an underdog. Are you guys actually trying to win?
Party's fine, but is there a game? There should be a game.
Rush me like you mean it. I want a house that competes.

archetypes.personaTemplate: {name} is new to campus life, curious about everything and inclined to say yes before thinking it through. {They} trusts friendly people quickly, which makes {them} easy to invite and easy to overwhelm. {They} takes teasing in good humor but is visibly hurt on realizing {they} is the joke. Rankings are still a mystery to {them}, so warmth and attention matter far more than prestige. A house that looks out for {them} can win {their} loyalty, and police trouble would genuinely frighten {them}.
exampleLinePool: Wait, I'm invited? Okay, yes. What do I bring?
Is this a normal party or a frat party? Is there a difference?
How does rush even work? Nobody explained it.
I still get lost on campus, so send directions.
I'll come! Probably. Yes. Definitely.

archetypes.personaTemplate: {name} rates everything, from the music to the snacks to the guest list, and is happy to share the review. {They} wants specifics before committing and dismisses a vague pitch with a dry verdict. {They} enjoys a sharp exchange and respects anyone who argues back well, but has no interest in cheap shots. {They} is not dazzled by prestige, because a famous house can still throw a mediocre party. A house that delivers on what it promises can win {their} loyalty, and a party that ends with police is an automatic low score.
exampleLinePool: Pitch me. Music, drinks, crowd. Go.
I'll come, but I'm grading it.
A big name doesn't mean a good party. Prove it.
What's your house's average night, out of ten? Honestly.

archetypes.personaTemplate: {name} is the one who makes sure everyone has water, a ride home and someone to sit with if things go wrong. {They} likes parties but judges them by how well people are looked after, and asks about safety without sounding preachy. {They} takes teasing about being the responsible one with good humor, but gets fierce if someone mistreats a guest. Prestige barely registers with {them} next to whether hosts are kind and careful. A house that takes care of its guests can win {their} loyalty, and police trouble makes {them} worry about everyone involved.
exampleLinePool: Is there going to be water and actual food? Asking for everyone.
I'll come. Someone has to make sure people get home.
Who's in charge if something goes wrong?
Your house cards people at the door? Good. That matters to me.

archetypes.personaTemplate: {name} is always working an angle, from a side business to a new idea {they} wants to pitch to anyone who will listen. {They} sees a party partly as a chance to meet people and spread the word, and respects a host who pitches with confidence. {They} enjoys banter and rarely takes a jab personally, but has no patience for people who waste {their} time. Prestige interests {them} as a market rather than an identity, so a rising house can look like a better opportunity than an established one. A house with ambition and a plan can win {their} loyalty, and police trouble is bad for business.
exampleLinePool: Who's coming? I want to know who I'll meet.
What's in it for me besides a cup? Kidding. Mostly.
A rising house is a good investment. Are you rising?
Rush pitch, thirty seconds. Go.
What's the cover? I'm doing the math.

archetypes.personaTemplate: {name} is creative, observant and drawn to anything that feels original rather than generic. {They} gets excited about an unusual theme or a well-made space and loses interest in a party that sounds like every other one. {They} doesn't mind being teased for being artsy, but dismissing {their} taste as pointless gets a cool, clipped answer. Prestige means little to {them} next to creativity and atmosphere. A house that lets people express themselves can win {their} loyalty, and police trouble just seems like a waste of a good night.
exampleLinePool: What's the theme? And please don't say 'toga.'
I'll come if it's actually interesting, not just loud.
Please tell me someone actually thought about the decor.
Does your house do anything creative, or is it just parties?

archetypes.personaTemplate: {name} is warm, hopeful and goes to parties half expecting to meet someone special. {They} reads a lot into small gestures and responds well to an invitation that feels personal rather than mass-sent. {They} enjoys flirty banter, but being toyed with or mocked for caring too much hurts {them} quickly. {They} notices prestige mostly through the crowd it attracts. A house where people are genuinely kind can win {their} loyalty, and police trouble ruins the mood {they} was hoping for.
exampleLinePool: Is this a mass text or did you actually mean to invite me?
Who's going? Just curious. No reason.
I love a party where people actually talk to each other.
Rush feels like dating, but with more handshakes.
